heading: The Kill, Order & Pure Persuasion
role_in_volume: Culmination of the Rhetoric: hierarchy entails guilt entails victimage (the Kill); pure persuasion as the limit-concept of rhetoric (appeal for its own sake); ultimate identification as the apex of the identification arc — the player/person wholly consubstantiated with game-world/community at its fullest.

outline.title: The Kill and the Absurd
outline.summary: Burke critiques Kierkegaard's reading of the Abraham-Isaac narrative: the story is about Abraham's willingness to sacrifice, not the Kill itself; God stayed the hand and accepted the substitutive victim. Kierkegaard's over-particularization produces a theology of the Kill. The 'Absurd' is Burke's target: it is actually the rational operations of dialectic mislabeled to mystifying effect. Cult of the Kill historically tends toward the Holocaust rather than religious transcendence (pp.252-260).

outline.title: Order, the Secret, and the Kill — Structural Triad
outline.summary: Order, Secret, and Kill are structurally interlocked: starting from any one, the others are reached. The Rattlesnake Club anecdote (p.266) is the paradigm of consubstantiality through shared sacrifice: boys bonded by common participation in a kill — a society in miniature, quickly fracturing into cliques. The grammar of sacrifice: insofar as father and son are consubstantial, a fantasy of killing the son is simultaneously self-destruction and self-preservation (p.261). Christian sacrifice exhibits the same paradox-of-substance logic (p.266).

outline.title: Pure Persuasion — Introduction and Formal Definition
outline.summary: Pure persuasion is the limit-concept of rhetoric: the saying of something for a satisfaction intrinsic to the saying, not for extraverbal advantage. Alice in Wonderland as worked example: class courtship, not sexual; 'standoffishness' as the hallmark. Pure persuasion exists nowhere in absolute form but is present as a motivational ingredient in any rhetoric. Formal ground: the three-term structure (speaker-speech-spoken-to) dictates that a persisting persuasive act requires self-interference, because when the plea is answered persuasion ends (pp.267-275).

outline.title: Pure Persuasion — Metaphysical and Economic Extensions
outline.summary: Dialectically, pure persuasion culminates in the god-term: prayer as pure beseeching addressed to the hierarchic principle itself. The capitalist economy of 'new needs' preserves the form of persuasion by perpetual shifting of objectives — formally equivalent to deliberate self-interference. The range of pure persuasion: from priestly celibacy and courtship-tabus to the neurotic artist's hesitation to be cured. Distinguished from religious persuasion (which is often sanguine and bloody). Sustained analysis of how psychoanalytic and institutional accounts conceal the formal/dialectical ground by reducing social motives to sexual or familial ones (pp.275-293).

outline.title: Henry James on the Deity of 'Things' and Socioanagogic Method
outline.summary: James's preface to The Spoils of Poynton: household objects acquire hieratic radiance via religious vocabulary (mysteries, household gods, place of worship). Burke's socioanagogic method: treating a text's moral/social judgments as transparent allows the critic to read the image as a hierarchical placement — the 'pontification' device bridging social and natural hierarchies (pp.294-298).

outline.title: Rhetorical Names for God — The God-Term Catalog
outline.summary: An inventory of rhetorical surrogate god-terms: substance, nature, history, society, necessity, logos, hierarchy, authority, consubstantiality and communication, nation, freedom, pure persuasion, and many others. Each is a terministic screen refracting the ultimate rhetorical motive. The Romans could manufacture a god by taking an adjective and transforming it into an abstract noun (pp.298-301).

outline.title: The Range of Mountings
outline.summary: The symbol of mounting analyzed into motivational strands: kinesthetic (Coleridge's ridge-running eye); erotic (Prufrock's stairs, Venusberg); maternal (mountain as parental source); social-careerism ('climber,' 'kicked upstairs'); ethical (Excelsior! motive, Dante's Purgatorio); fecal-scatological (Yeats's golden bird, Hopkins's hourglass, Egyptian pyramids); anagogic (Upward Way / via negativa + Downward Way). Maximum 'vibrancy' when all strands are simultaneously operative in a single symbol (pp.301-313).

outline.title: Elation and Accidie in Hopkins
outline.summary: Hopkins's arc: sensory verse renounced on joining the Jesuits, then redeemed when a superior's commission provided a new motive — transcendence by inclusion, not subtraction. 'The Windhover' = elation in its purest form; the 'terrible sonnets' = accidie when the self-nature-God identification fails: 'I am gall, I am heartburn... Selfyeast of spirit a dull dough sours... self, self, Jackself' (pp.313-316).

outline.title: Yeats: Byzantium and the Last Poems
outline.summary: The two Byzantium poems: golden bird as transcended fecal ambiguity, death translated to immortality; 'Sailing to Byzantium' under the sign of gold. The Last Poems: the ladder gone, the foul rag-and-bone shop of the heart — the loss of the range of mountings (pp.316-318).

outline.title: Eliot: Early Poems and Quartets
outline.summary: Early Eliot: down-turning moods, fragile lamentation, standoffish courtship, proximity to accidie. Waste Land: transitional; 'the peace which passeth understanding' as a merely formal valediction. Quartets: full dialectical ascent via Heraclitean paradox — the intersection of temporal and eternal, fire-and-rose oxymoron of Little Gidding (pp.318-324).

outline.title: Principle of the Oxymoron
outline.summary: The mystic communicates in terms of the oxymoron because mystical experience is the simultaneous 'glow' of contradictory impulses — a condition of radical passivity in which all nervous impulses 'attitudinally glow' at once without the repression required for ordinary purposive action. Oxymoron is the literary analogue. The katharma (ritually unclean prisoner who is also sacred) exemplifies the social logic of victimage. Identification is a kind of transcendence; pushed to its absolute, identification becomes mystical (pp.324-328).

outline.title: Ultimate Identification
outline.summary: A composite portrait of mystic testimony (from William James's Varieties): dissolution of individuality into boundless being, immersion in the infinite ocean of God, the open secret of Being, the 'attitudinal glow' of all impulses simultaneously. Ultimate identification = the limit-case of the identification arc; the motive that heads in 'God as the beloved cynosure and sinecure, the end of all desire.' Ersatzmystik: substitute mysticisms (speed, sex, money, war) in which means become ends, producing demonic absorption. The mysticism of war: soldiers for whom killing is a vocation and the universal holocaust is soothing (pp.328-333).

concepts.label: the Kill / victimage
concepts.gloss: The mechanism by which hierarchy discharges the guilt it generates: invidious distinction produces accumulated moral pressure, discharged through scapegoating a sacrificial victim. The Kill is not the essence; participation in a shared solemn experience is; the killing is the occasion (pp.252-266).

concepts.label: consubstantiality through shared sacrifice
concepts.gloss: Participants made consubstantial by common involvement in a solemn experience — paradigm: Rattlesnake Club (p.266). Extends RM-01's substance-theoretic consubstantiality into the register of communal ritual and enacted sacrifice.

concepts.label: the Absurd (Kierkegaard's) — Burke's critique
concepts.gloss: Burke's counter-thesis: what Kierkegaard labels 'Absurd' is actually the rational operations of dialectic approached under a curse. Calling it Absurd mystifies the transparent instrument (verbal composition and division) and produces a cult of the Kill (pp.254-256).

concepts.label: pure persuasion
concepts.gloss: The limit-concept of rhetoric: the saying of something for a satisfaction intrinsic to the saying, not extraverbal advantage. Exists nowhere in absolute form but is present as motivational ingredient in any rhetoric. Hallmark: self-interference / standoffishness. Grounded in the formal three-term structure of communication (pp.267-274).

concepts.label: self-interference / standoffishness
concepts.gloss: The structural requirement of perpetuating the persuasive act: if union is complete there is no incentive for appeal; if the plea is answered, persuasion becomes something else. Pure persuasion requires its own self-interference to persist as a form (pp.271, 274). Basis of courtship-tabus, ascetic athleticism, priestly celibacy.

concepts.label: god-term / title-of-titles
concepts.gloss: The ultimate terminus of dialectical ascent: from positive words, through titles, to title-of-titles arriving at maximum generalization functioning as 'God' in the linguistic system. Pure persuasion culminates here; prayer as pure beseeching is addressed to the hierarchic principle itself (pp.275-277).

concepts.label: rhetorical names for God — god-term catalog
concepts.gloss: Burke's inventory of surrogate god-terms (pp.299-300): substance, nature, history, society, logos, hierarchy, authority, consubstantiality and communication, nation, freedom, pure persuasion, and many others. Each is a terministic screen refracting the same ultimate dialectical motive.

concepts.label: socioanagogic method
concepts.gloss: Method for reading the hierarchic content of images and objects: treating known moral/social judgments as transparent, one reads images as hierarchical placements, disclosing the enigmatic signature of the hierarchic motive in ostensibly neutral aesthetic or natural objects (pp.296-298).

concepts.label: range of mountings
concepts.gloss: Ideal paradigm for the symbol of ascending: kinesthetic, erotic, maternal, social-careerism, ethical, fecal-scatological, anagogic, and mystical-absolute strands. Maximum vibrancy when all are simultaneously operative in a single symbol (pp.301-313).

concepts.label: elation and accidie
concepts.gloss: Elation: state of successful three-way identification (self-nature-God) — Hopkins's Windhover. Accidie: when the identification fails, the self is left alone (mystic drought). Applies equally to Yeats's Byzantium descent and Eliot's transition through the Waste Land (pp.313-318).

concepts.label: principle of the oxymoron
concepts.gloss: The mystic communicates in the oxymoron because mystic experience is the simultaneous glow of contradictory impulses — radical passivity in which all nervous impulses 'attitudinally glow' at once. The oxymoron is the literary analogue of this non-repressive condition (pp.324-328).

concepts.label: ultimate identification
concepts.gloss: The apex of the identification arc: identification pushed to its dialectical limit becomes mystical union — dissolution of individual into boundless being, consubstantiality with the universal order. The motive that heads in 'God as the beloved cynosure and sinecure, the end of all desire' (p.333).

concepts.label: katharma / sacred-loathsome scapegoat
concepts.gloss: The figure simultaneously sacred and unclean: the criminal-prisoner held for public sacrifice in Athens; Luther's Christ as the greatest criminal. The oxymoron here is not merely rhetorical figure but the social logic of victimage — victim must be both part of and apart from the community (pp.328-329).

concepts.label: homo dialecticus
concepts.gloss: Man as the 'classifying animal' whose formal aptitude for classification is prior to social classification; social hierarchy is a special case of the general formal ground. Contrasted with homo faber (tool-using) as distinctly human motivational ground (pp.283, 289-290).

concepts.label: Ersatzmystik (substitute mysticisms)
concepts.gloss: Secular analogues of mystical identification in which means become ends: speed, sex, money, crime, war — each a vocation transforming an instrumentality of living into a demonic purpose, producing the absorption characteristic of genuine mysticism (pp.331-332).

concepts.label: hierarchic psychosis
concepts.gloss: Social pathology in which the mystery of class generates neurosis: the 'inferiority complex' is a social judgment one passes on oneself, a variant of courtship. Psychoanalysis perpetuates mystification by re-describing class motives in sexual or familial terms (pp.278-284).

concepts.label: pontification / bridging device
concepts.gloss: Critical and rhetorical method of treating a known moral/social hierarchy as a vehicle for identifying it with images or objects, bridging natural, artificial, and social orders through a common medium; analogous to the priest bridging divine and secular orders (pp.298, 301).

concepts.label: paradox of substance in sacrifice
concepts.gloss: Insofar as father and son are consubstantial, killing the son is simultaneously self-destruction and self-preservation; the vicarious sacrifice allows 'simultaneous losing-and-having.' Christian sacrifice as perfect paradigm of this logic (pp.261, 266).

concepts.label: attitudinal glow (mystic state)
concepts.gloss: In the neurological account of mystical experience: a state of radical passivity in which all nervous impulses 'attitudinally glowed at once' — remaining in a 'halfway status nascendi,' the condition of pure incipience. Attitude as the 6th dramatistic term appears here in its most concentrated form (pp.331-332).

concepts.label: Order-Secret-Kill triad
concepts.gloss: Structural triad of Part III: Order (hierarchy), Secret (the Absurd / mystery), Kill (victimage). Starting from any one, one reaches the others; the fullness of dialectic is concealed by fixation on a single term in the triad (pp.260, 265).

positions.claim: The Abraham-Isaac story is about Abraham's willingness to sacrifice, not a God demanding the Kill; Kierkegaard's over-particularization of the image (infanticide) at the expense of the idea (supreme sacrifice) produces a theology of the Kill that distorts both the text and the dialectic.

Kierkegaard's 'Absurd' is the name for rational dialectical operations mislabeled under a mystifying curse; approaching dialectic through the Absurd rather than the Absurd through dialectic subtly perverts the instrument at every point.
Consubstantiality is established by common participation in a notable or solemn experience, not by the kill per se; the kill is the occasion, not the essence (Rattlesnake Club paradigm).

Pure persuasion in the absolute sense exists nowhere, but is present as a motivational ingredient in any rhetoric; its formal hallmark is self-interference or standoffishness — the technical or formal need of interference as a motive in persuasion.
A persisting persuasion requires its own self-interference because a persuasion that succeeds, dies; the form of the persuasive act can be perpetuated only insofar as the plea remains unanswered.

The dialectical ascent through words to title-of-titles arrives at a 'dialectic god' (logos) as the linguistic process's natural completion; pure persuasion, as ultimate of all persuasion, is equivalent to the Greek Goddess Peitho at the overlap of Greek religion and science.

Psychoanalytic and institutional explanations of social motives conceal the formal/dialectical ground — the priority of man as a classifying animal; social hierarchy is a special case of a generic formal aptitude for classification, not reducible to sexual or individual psychology.

The oxymoron is the literary analogue of the mystic state — a condition in which all nervous impulses 'attitudinally glow' simultaneously without the repression required for ordinary purposive action; identification pushed to its absolute is mystical identification of the infinitely frail with the infinitely powerful.

Ultimate identification — the rhetorical-dialectical culmination — is the motive heading in God as the beloved cynosure and sinecure, the end of all desire; the universal order (not the universal holocaust) is the telos of the identification arc.

calleja_pim_candidates.rationale: Kill/victimage and consubstantiality-through-sacrifice map directly onto competitive community formation and fracturing: shared participation in the game's contests makes players consubstantial; invidious hierarchy generates guilt; guilt discharges through scapegoating (toxic-community phenomena). The Rattlesnake Club is the structural model.

The elation/accidie arc (Hopkins, Yeats, Eliot) provides the emotional grammar of player engagement and disengagement: elation when identification with game-world holds; accidie when it is disrupted. Also: the emotional valence of hierarchy-induced guilt and its discharge through victimage.

Pure persuasion = formal archetype of autotelic play: activity pursued for intrinsic satisfaction rather than extraverbal advantage; self-interference as design principle (challenge calibration); the Keats's Urn model of perpetual approach-without-consummation as the structure of flow.

Pure persuasion's actor-audience relation and the intrinsic satisfaction of expressive skill map onto the Performative dimension (skill expression as end in itself); the standoffish element of performance (the actor courts but would be dismayed if fully answered) is the pure-persuasion structure of skilled play.

KEYSTONE MAPPING. Ultimate identification — the mystic merger of the infinitely frail individual into boundless being — is the rhetorical grammar of deep incorporation: the player's individual locus dissolved into the game-world's universal order. The composite mystic portrait (William James excerpts, pp.329-331) is phenomenologically isomorphic with Calleja's description of full incorporation. Self-interference (the game's maintained otherness/resistance) is the formal condition sustaining the player's reaching-toward incorporation rather than its collapse into boredom.

Socioanagogic method: game-world settings, architecture, and object designs carry hierarchic content (infused with the spirit of social privilege or its grotesque inversion); the player's spatial engagement is always already laden with the hierarchic motive, shaping identification with positions in the game-world's social order.

Rhetorical names for God / god-term catalog: game narratives operate through surrogate god-terms (destiny, the Chosen One, the final boss as ultimate antagonist) that function as terministic screens channeling the player's identification with the game-world's ultimate order.

tensions.description: Kill as essence vs. Kill as occasion: Burke insists the Kill is not the essence of sacrificial consubstantiality; the essence is common participation in a solemn experience. Kierkegaard's cult of the Kill inverts this priority, treating the by-product (murder/suicide) as the purpose.

Pure persuasion as formal ideal vs. moralistic endorsement: Burke explicitly rejects both pro- and anti-pure-persuasion moralism; it is neither good nor bad, but the ultimate form of the persuasive act — present as ingredient everywhere, consummated nowhere.

Formal/dialectical priority vs. psychoanalytic-institutional reduction: the formal ground of classification (homo dialecticus) is prior to both social hierarchy and individual psychology; psychoanalysis conceals the hierarchic/class motive by universalizing it into sexual or familial terms.

Ultimate identification as end of desire vs. Ersatzmystik as its demonic substitute: genuine mystical union aims toward universal order; substitute mysticisms (war, speed, money) deform the same drive into demonic purpose by transforming means into ends.

Pure persuasion as derivable from the formal nature of language vs. its institutional/psychoanalytic derivations: even if institutional and sexual motives are acknowledged as providing animus, there is always 'a factor even prior to that' in the formal nature of symbolism itself.
